key_insight: A deep learning surrogate can replace expensive crystal plasticity simulations to optimize polycrystalline microstructures for competing strength targets while preserving full-field dynamic response information.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid, physics-informed materials design for impact-resistant metals, cutting optimization cost by orders of magnitude without sacrificing validation accuracy.
method: 3D U-Net maps polycrystalline copper microstructures to full-field velocity histories from plate-impact simulations.
Stochastic microstructure generation is paired with derivative-free optimization to search the design space.
A distribution-consistent reliability region (DCRR) using MMD monitors surrogate validity during optimization.
evidence_signal: Across multiple design cases, optimized microstructures were validated by CPFE with less than 3% prediction error, while cumulative evaluation time dropped by about four orders of magnitude.
watch_item: Reliability depends on staying within the surrogate’s training distribution, so distribution shift must be monitored carefully during optimization.
paper_title: Deep learning driven framework for optimization of polycrystalline microstructures under competing strength requirements
